$schemaComment: Runtime-consumed release automation config. Only `anchorPackages` is read at runtime, by release_nuget.verify_public_receipt(): the exact three packages fully downloaded, hash-verified, and dotnet-signature-verified for every 'finish plan'/'finish apply', regardless of release version. Every other required SkiaSharp/HarfBuzzSharp-family package ID -- and the version it must carry -- is derived per release from scripts/VERSIONS.txt at the exact source commit the SkiaSharp anchor's own nuspec embeds (see release_nuget.read_family_ids_at_commit), never from a static list in this file. A static family list here previously implied it was authoritative for verifying any release, which it can never safely be for an already-published, older version: a package introduced to VERSIONS.txt after that version shipped never existed on NuGet.org for it, and polling for it would eventually and incorrectly time out. tests/test_release_nuget.py's PublicPackagesManifestTests cross-checks anchorPackages against the *current* scripts/VERSIONS.txt (so a newly introduced anchor candidate is never silently missed) as a maintenance-time sanity check only -- it has no bearing on verifying any specific release and is not consulted at runtime.
